PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MINUTES
  NOVEMBER 4, 2019

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274, by CHAIR ZIGRANG.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR ZIGRANG led those assembled in the salute to the flag.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONER’S PRESENT:  Schachter, Scott, Zigrang, Carman, Yoo, Edler

  COMMISSIONER’S ABSENT:  Medawar

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 7, 2019.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 7,
  2019.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6-A

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-17-19; APPLICANT: Mr. Mark Teneyck; LOCATION:
  28 Encanto Drive, Rolling Hills Estates; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination is requested for one and two-story additions to a single-story residence.

  Associate Planner Thom presented a PowerPoint presentation for Planning Application No. PA-
  17-19 summarizing the staff report.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
  Planning Application No. PA-17-19 with the conditions noted in the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about the ground floor plan that does not show the wall between
  the house and the garage or where to access the stairs.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  1
MINUTES, NOVEMBER 4, 2019
   Mark Teneyck, Property Owners, stated that there will be a fire wall installed (per code) between
  the house and the garage for stairway access.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-17-19 AS PRESENTED.

  Ayes: Schachter, Scott, Zigrang, Carman, Yoo, Edler
  Noes:
  Absent: Medawar
  Abstain:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that there is a 20-day approval period for this item.

  B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-18-19; APPLICANT: Ms. Saghik Wartan; LOCATION:
  3 Clear Vista Drive, Rolling Hills Estates; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination is requested for one and two-story additions to a single-story residence.

  Commissioner Yoo recused himself from this item due to being within a 500’ radius of the subject
  property.

  Associate Planner Thom presented a PowerPoint presentation for Planning Application No. PA-
  18-19 summarizing the staff report.

  In response to a question by CHAIR ZIGRANG, Associate Planner Thom stated that both
  balconies were included in the last proposal.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that this home violates City Councils’ guideline on the size of
  homes, by 15%, and it appears that this did not change from the previous proposal. Associate
  Planner Thom stated that this home has been slightly reduced by 16 sq. ft.

  Sina Khajavi, SK Architects, stated that since the last proposal, the entry tower has been
  eliminated and a covered entry porch was added which contributed to visually breaking up the
  building height. A neighbor expressed their concerns regarding the terrace, and the property
  owner has since eliminated the terrace and scaled back the chimney. Mr. Khajavi provided
  addresses for similar sized homes in the neighborhood and stated that this neighborhood has
  numerous larger homes.

  CHAIR ZIGRANG regarding the chimney facing 5 Clear Vista and asked if the fireplace can
  become a direct vent. Mr. Khajavi agreed.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER asked about the square footage of the new plan. Mr. Khajavi
  stated that the square footage did not change.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the concerns with the last proposal was mass the
  mass and density. The mass has been addressed by making it look like two stories which makes
  it compatible with other homes in the neighborhood. COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that
  he is still concerned with the size of the project and prefers that it be reduced to 5,000 sq. ft. or
  less.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that this is still in violation of the City Councils’ guideline on
  home size and if approved, he requested, that it be flagged by Planning staff to the City Council
  to consider how they feel about the guideline.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER agreed with COMMISSIONER SCOTT and stated that if approved, this
  should be flagged to the City Council.

  VICE CHAIR CARMAN stated that she is not in favor of this design due to the scale, however,
  stated that she appreciates the changes that were made to the front of the property.

  CHAIR ZIGRANG stated that this is more than the guidelines but the architect has done a good
  job compartmentalizing the project. He stated that he would prefer to see this home at 5,000 sq.
  ft. but it is difficult to require this since there are similar sized homes in this neighborhood.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  2
MINUTES, NOVEMBER 4, 2019
   In response to a question by CHAIR ZIGRANG, Planning Manager Naughton stated that this can
  be taken to the City Council as an informational item and they may choose to pull the item and
  put it on their agenda for review prior to the appeal period. If this is done, the City Council could
  make a decision to approve or deny a project.

  COMMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that this does not seem totally out of place in this
  neighborhood.

  CHAIR ZIGRANG added that the Homeowners Association in this neighborhood supports this
  project.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-18-19 WITH NO WESTERN
  ELEVATION OUTDOOR TERRACE AND WITH A DIRECT VENT CHIMNEY.

  Ayes: Schachter, Scott, Zigrang, Edler
  Noes: Carman
  Absent: Medawar
  Abstain: Yoo

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that there is a 20-day approval period for this item.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT move approval COMMISSIONER EDLER.

  C.  ROOF MATERIAL STANDARDS STUDY SESSION

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff made an effort to find a different metrics to measure
  thickness and was not able to find an alternative. Therefore, staff is recommending no changes
  to the Municipal Code. However, staff has learned that the intention of the Planning Commission
  was not to take such a conservative approach when applying the code and rather to look for a
  quarter inch on any part of the application. Staff has been requiring that the shingle be a quarter
  inch all around which limits options.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that if the Planning Commission is in agreement, staff will
  take a more liberal approach when approving asphalt shingles and will provide additional options
  for residents.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that staff would still like direction on roofing colors.

  The Planning Commission inspected the roofing material samples provided by staff.

  VICE CHAIR CARMAN agreed with the difficulty in establishing a metric for acceptable materials
  and stated that staff requested more direction on color. She suggested that staff have a list of
  approved colors.

  CHAIR ZIGRANG agreed that a list of acceptable colors would be helpful and if a resident
  proposed a color that is not on the list, they would have the option to bring it before the Planning
  Commission for review. The Planning Commissioners agreed.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff will work on an expanded list of roofing materials
  with colors.

  The Planning Commission agreed on a more relaxed approval process for measuring roof
  thickness.

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  3
MINUTES, NOVEMBER 4, 2019
   9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT inquired about 1 Encanto. Planning Manager Naughton stated that this
  case is still on hold pending final decision on acceptable roofing colors and staff is still in
  discussion regarding enforcement.

  10.  MANAGER’S ITEMS

  A.  REGIONAL HOUSING NEEDS ASSESSMENT (RHNA) UPDATE.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided an overview and update on Regional Housing Needs
  Assessment (RHNA) and stated that the Planning Commission will continue to be updated. This
  will also come up when the Planning Commission reviews the Housing Element as well as policies
  that may need to be updated.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER EDLER, Planning Manager Naughton stated that
  the City’s Housing Element needs to be certified by HCD, the City would need to set-up structure
  for the required type of housing to be built.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about the consequences if a developer is not interested in
  building this type of housing. Planning Manager Naughton stated that she does not think that the
  State would take any enforcement action as long as the city has a Housing Element that is in
  compliance.

  In response to a question by VICE CHAIR CARMAN, Planning Manager Naughton stated that
  housing is not restricted to ownership units. She also explained the challenges with capturing
  ADU’s to include in affordable housing numbers.

  B.  NEW HOUSING LAWS

  Planning Manager Naughton provided an update on the new housing laws, which will go into
  effect January 1, 2020. There were eighteen new housing related bills, which includes five
  specifically related to ADU’s.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that a new Housing Element and changes in the Zoning
  Ordinance will be coming before the Planning Commission in 2020.

  The Planning Commission held a brief discussion and expressed their concerns with these new
  housing bills.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, OCTOBER 22, 2019

  B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES, OCTOBER 21, 2019

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A – 11B.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ZIGRANG adjourned the meeting at 8:50 p.m. The next Planning Commission meeting
  will be held on Monday, December 2, 2019 at 7:00 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,

  ______________________________  _____________________________
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Heidi Luce, City Clerk
